title: Finite coefficient module pullback and its canonical generators
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its fixed uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $n\in\mathbf N$, with level $n$ denoting positive exponent $n+1$. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^{n+1})$ and let $B_{W,n}$ be its constant sheaf of rings on the small pro-etale site of $W$. Use the canonical pro-etale inverse image, the base-change functor $u_f$, and its constant-section ring map $c^f_{A_n}:f^{-1}B_{Y,n}\to B_{X,n}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define the finite module pullback functor by $f_n^*M=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}B_{Y,n}}B_{X,n}$, with its canonical action on module maps. Equivalently it is the canonical left adjoint to the sectionwise direct image with coefficient action restricted along the constant-section map $B_{Y,n}\to f_*B_{X,n}$. For a $B_{Y,n}$-module sheaf $M$, an object $V$ of the small pro-etale site of $Y$, and $x\in M(V)$, define its pullback generator to be $\eta_{f_n,M,V}(x)\in(f_n^*M)(u_f(V))$, where $\eta$ is the unit of this fixed pullback/direct-image adjunction. In tensor notation it is $f^{-1}(x)\otimes1$. The scheme universe and coefficient universe are independent; there is no invertibility, flatness, boundedness, constructibility or finite-field hypothesis.
